title: Quality Review & Accountability
outline: NAHQ CPHQ Detailed Content Outline (2024 R2b, in 2026 handbook)

questions.task_name: Apply standards, best practices, and other information from quality-related organizations
questions.stem: A hospital decides to adopt an externally published, evidence-based sepsis guideline. What should the quality professional do FIRST?

options.A: Rewrite all sepsis policies word for word
options.B: Do a gap analysis of current practice against the guideline
options.C: Begin auditing physician compliance with the new guideline immediately
options.D: Purchase an electronic sepsis alert system to enforce the guideline

questions.explanation_en: Applying external best practice starts with understanding where current practice differs (gap analysis). Policy rewrites, audits, and technology come after gaps and priorities are known.
questions.explanation_ar: أول خطوة لتطبيق دليل خارجي هي تحليل الفجوة بين الممارسة الحالية والتوصيات.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: clinical practice guidelines, pathways, and outcomes
questions.stem: Which statement BEST distinguishes a clinical pathway from a clinical practice guideline?

options.A: A pathway is a legally binding standard, while a guideline is optional
options.B: A pathway is written by physicians, while a guideline is written by nurses
options.C: A multidisciplinary, time-sequenced plan that puts a guideline into practice
options.D: A pathway applies to all inpatients regardless of their diagnosis

questions.explanation_en: Guidelines give evidence-based recommendations; pathways translate them into a day-by-day / step-by-step multidisciplinary care plan for a specific population. Neither is automatically legally binding.
questions.explanation_ar: المسار السريري خطة متعددة التخصصات ومتسلسلة زمنياً تُطبّق توصيات الدليل.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: clinical practice guidelines, pathways, and outcomes
questions.stem: During pathway monitoring, 18% of patients deviate from the expected day-3 discharge. What is the MOST appropriate response?

options.A: Analyze variance reasons: patient, practitioner, and system
options.B: Remove variance cases from the data
options.C: Require all practitioners to follow the pathway with no exceptions
options.D: Discontinue the pathway because compliance is below the 85% target

questions.explanation_en: Variance analysis is the purpose of pathway monitoring. Some variance is clinically justified (patient-driven); system-driven variances are the main improvement opportunities. Excluding data or forbidding all deviation is inappropriate.
questions.explanation_ar: حلّل أسباب الانحرافات (مريض، ممارس، نظام) ولا تحذفها من البيانات.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: quality-based payment programs
questions.stem: Under a quality-based payment program, a hospital's Medicare payments are reduced because its risk-adjusted 30-day readmission ratios exceed expected levels. Which program is this?

options.A: Hospital-Acquired Condition Reduction Program
options.B: Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS)
options.C: Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting pay-for-reporting
options.D: Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program (HRRP)

questions.explanation_en: HRRP adjusts payment for excess readmissions for selected conditions/procedures. HACRP targets hospital-acquired conditions; MIPS applies to clinicians; pay-for-reporting rewards submission, not performance.
questions.explanation_ar: برنامج HRRP يخفض المدفوعات بسبب زيادة حالات إعادة الدخول.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: quality-based payment programs
questions.stem: In a value-based purchasing model that awards points for both achievement and improvement, how is a measure typically scored?

options.A: The higher of the achievement score or the improvement score
options.B: Only improvement compared with the prior year's performance counts
options.C: The achievement and improvement scores are multiplied together
options.D: Only achievement against the national top-decile benchmark counts

questions.explanation_en: Achievement-and-improvement designs reward both high performers and organizations improving from a low baseline, usually by taking the higher of the two scores.
questions.explanation_ar: يحصل المستشفى على الأعلى بين درجة الإنجاز ودرجة التحسن.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: documentation
questions.stem: A hospital's risk-adjusted mortality index (observed/expected) is unexpectedly high. Chart review shows comorbidities are often not documented. What is the MOST likely effect?

options.A: Observed mortality is overstated, which inflates the O/E ratio
options.B: Expected mortality is understated, which inflates the O/E ratio
options.C: The ratio is unaffected because risk models use vital signs only
options.D: Expected mortality is overstated, which artificially lowers the ratio

questions.explanation_en: Risk models rely on coded diagnoses. Missing comorbidities make patients look healthier than they are, so expected deaths fall and O/E rises. Documentation improvement is a quality-data issue, not just billing.
questions.explanation_ar: نقص توثيق الأمراض المصاحبة يقلل الوفيات المتوقعة فيرتفع مؤشر O/E.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: practitioner performance evaluation
questions.stem: A surgeon is newly granted privileges to perform robotic procedures. Which process is required?

options.A: Ongoing Professional Practice Evaluation (OPPE) only
options.B: External peer review
options.C: Focused Professional Practice Evaluation (FPPE)
options.D: Summary suspension pending competence review

questions.explanation_en: FPPE applies to new privileges (and to concerns about a practitioner's performance). OPPE is the continuous monitoring of all privileged practitioners. External review and suspension are not routine for new privileges.
questions.explanation_ar: الامتيازات الجديدة تتطلب تقييماً مركزاً FPPE.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: practitioner performance evaluation
questions.stem: Which characteristic is MOST important for an effective and fair peer review process?

options.A: Review by the department chair alone
options.B: Review limited to cases that have resulted in malpractice lawsuits
options.C: Publishing individual review outcomes to all medical staff
options.D: Peers with relevant expertise using predefined criteria

questions.explanation_en: Credible peer review uses appropriate peers, standardized criteria/case selection, timeliness, and confidentiality. Single-reviewer, litigation-only, or public disclosure models undermine fairness and protection.
questions.explanation_ar: مراجعة الأقران العادلة تتم بأقران مختصين ومعايير محددة مسبقاً.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: patient experience
questions.stem: Which survey item measures patient EXPERIENCE rather than patient SATISFACTION?

options.A: "How often did nurses explain things in a way you could understand?"
options.B: "How satisfied were you overall with the quality of the hospital food?"
options.C: "Would you rate your stay as excellent compared with other hospitals?"
options.D: "How pleased were you with the comfort and cleanliness of your room?"

questions.explanation_en: Experience items ask whether/how often something happened (reportable events of care). Satisfaction items ask whether expectations were met. Standardized surveys such as HCAHPS emphasize experience.
questions.explanation_ar: أسئلة التجربة تسأل ماذا حدث وكم مرة، لا مدى الرضا.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: patient experience
questions.stem: A patient complains verbally to the charge nurse about delayed pain medication, and the issue cannot be resolved before the patient asks for a formal response. How should this be handled?

options.A: Treat it as a compliment opportunity and close the case
options.B: Treat it as a grievance and follow the formal grievance process
options.C: Log it only as an informal complaint because it was made verbally
options.D: Refer it to risk management and take no further action on the unit

questions.explanation_en: A complaint that is not resolved promptly by staff present (or where a written response is requested) becomes a grievance with formal timelines and written response. Verbal vs written is not the deciding factor.
questions.explanation_ar: الشكوى غير المحلولة أو التي يُطلب لها رد رسمي تُعامل كتظلّم رسمي.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: identification of reportable events for accreditation and regulatory bodies
questions.stem: Under The Joint Commission definition, which outcome classifies a patient safety event as a sentinel event?

options.A: Any medication error that reaches the patient
options.B: A near miss involving a high-alert medication
options.C: Severe temporary harm to the patient
options.D: Any patient fall

questions.explanation_en: Sentinel events result in death, permanent harm, or severe temporary harm (plus certain listed events). Many errors, near misses and falls without such harm are not sentinel events.
questions.explanation_ar: الحدث الجسيم يشمل الوفاة أو الضرر الدائم أو الضرر المؤقت الشديد.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: identification of reportable events for accreditation and regulatory bodies
questions.stem: A quality manager identifies an event that meets the state health department's mandatory reporting criteria. What is the BEST action?

options.A: Delay reporting until the root cause analysis has been completed
options.B: Report only if the patient's family files a formal complaint
options.C: Report only to the accrediting body, since it supersedes the state
options.D: Report to the state on time while the internal review continues

questions.explanation_en: Mandatory reporting timelines run independently of internal analysis. External reporting obligations to regulators and accreditors are separate; one does not replace the other.
questions.explanation_ar: أبلغ الجهة الرسمية في الموعد المطلوب دون انتظار انتهاء التحليل الداخلي.

questions.task_name: Maintain confidentiality of performance/quality improvement records and reports
questions.stem: Which action is MOST likely to jeopardize legal protection of peer review/QI findings?

options.A: Filing committee conclusions in the patient's medical record
options.B: Labeling the report 'Confidential – Quality Improvement Work Product'
options.C: Restricting access to committee members with a need to know
options.D: Storing minutes in a secured, access-controlled QI database

questions.explanation_en: Protection is preserved by keeping QI/peer review documents separate, labeled, and access-restricted. Putting them in the medical record (a discoverable business record) can waive protection.
questions.explanation_ar: وضع نتائج مراجعة الأقران في الملف الطبي قد يُسقط الحماية القانونية.

questions.task_name: Maintain confidentiality of performance/quality improvement records and reports
questions.stem: An analyst requests patient-level data for a falls project. Which principle should guide the data release?

options.A: Full access – QI staff are entitled to view the entire medical record
options.B: Minimum necessary – only required elements, de-identified if possible
options.C: Patient consent must be obtained in writing for every QI data use
options.D: No release – any QI data use is prohibited by federal privacy law

questions.explanation_en: Privacy rules generally permit use of PHI for healthcare operations such as QI, but limited to the minimum necessary. Individual consent is not normally required for internal operations.
questions.explanation_ar: مبدأ الحد الأدنى الضروري مع إزالة الهوية قدر الإمكان.

questions.task_name: Maintain confidentiality of performance/quality improvement records and reports
questions.stem: In the United States, which law created federal privilege and confidentiality protections for patient safety work product reported to a Patient Safety Organization?

options.A: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996
options.B: Health Care Quality Improvement Act of 1986
options.C: Patient Safety and Quality Improvement Act of 2005
options.D: Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act

questions.explanation_en: PSQIA (2005) established PSOs and privilege for patient safety work product. HCQIA (1986) gives immunity for good-faith peer review and created the NPDB; HIPAA addresses privacy/security; EMTALA addresses emergency screening.
questions.explanation_ar: قانون PSQIA لعام 2005 أنشأ منظمات سلامة المرضى وحماية منتجات عملها.

questions.task_name: Implement and evaluate quality initiatives that impact reimbursement
questions.stem: Why is the Present on Admission (POA) indicator important for quality-related reimbursement?

options.A: It determines the patient's admission priority and bed placement
options.B: It identifies patients who are eligible for observation status
options.C: It replaces risk adjustment in hospital mortality models entirely
options.D: It separates hospital-acquired conditions, which may not be paid

questions.explanation_en: POA coding separates pre-existing conditions from hospital-acquired conditions; certain HACs not present on admission do not increase payment and feed penalty programs. Accurate POA documentation protects both data and revenue.
questions.explanation_ar: مؤشر POA يميز الحالات المكتسبة في المستشفى التي قد لا يُدفع مقابلها.

questions.task_name: Implement and evaluate quality initiatives that impact reimbursement
questions.stem: A CLABSI reduction project prevented 6 infections this year. Which calculation BEST demonstrates its financial impact?

options.A: (Infections avoided × cost per infection) − project cost
options.B: Central lines inserted × supply cost
options.C: Total hospital revenue ÷ number of infections reported this year
options.D: Staff hours spent on the project × average hourly wage of the team

questions.explanation_en: Return on investment compares avoided cost of poor quality with the cost of the intervention. The other options measure activity or inputs only.
questions.explanation_ar: العائد = التكلفة المتجنبة ناقص تكلفة المشروع.

questions.task_name: Apply standards, best practices, and other information from quality-related organizations
questions.stem: Which organization develops the Patient Safety Indicators (PSIs) that use administrative (claims) data to flag potential in-hospital complications?

options.A: Institute for Healthcare Improvement (IHI)
options.B: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
options.C: World Health Organization (WHO) Patient Safety
options.D: The Leapfrog Group hospital safety grade program

questions.explanation_en: AHRQ Quality Indicators include PSIs, IQIs, PQIs and PDIs. IHI provides improvement methods/campaigns; WHO publishes global safety guidance; Leapfrog publishes hospital safety grades using multiple sources.
questions.explanation_ar: وكالة AHRQ تطوّر مؤشرات سلامة المرضى PSIs.

questions.task_name: Apply standards, best practices, and other information from quality-related organizations
questions.stem: A hospital compares its surgical-site infection rate with a national benchmark. What is ESSENTIAL for a valid comparison?

options.A: Using a larger sample than the one used to build the benchmark
options.B: Excluding high-risk patients
options.C: Same measure definitions and appropriate risk adjustment
options.D: Comparing only to hospitals located in the same city or region

questions.explanation_en: Valid benchmarking requires identical numerator/denominator definitions and adjustment for case mix. Selectively excluding high-risk patients biases results.
questions.explanation_ar: المقارنة المرجعية تتطلب تعريفات موحدة وتعديلاً للمخاطر.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: practitioner performance evaluation
questions.stem: Which data set is MOST appropriate for Ongoing Professional Practice Evaluation (OPPE) of a hospitalist?

options.A: Hospital-wide patient satisfaction scores for the medicine service
options.B: Number of hours worked and shifts covered by the hospitalist per month
options.C: Department budget variance and supply costs for the quarter
options.D: Practitioner-specific indicators compared with peers over time

questions.explanation_en: OPPE uses practitioner-specific data relevant to the privileges held (e.g., outcomes, LOS, readmissions, guideline adherence, peer review results), trended and compared to defined targets/peers.
questions.explanation_ar: تقييم OPPE يعتمد على مؤشرات خاصة بالممارس ومقارنتها بالأقران.

questions.task_name: Apply standards, best practices, and other information from quality-related organizations
questions.stem: A hospital wants to adopt best practices for reducing catheter-associated urinary tract infections. Which source is MOST appropriate?

options.A: Evidence-based guidance such as CDC/HICPAC or IHI bundles
options.B: A single vendor's marketing study
options.C: Practices copied from the nearest hospital without evidence review
options.D: An internal opinion survey of staff about what they think works

questions.explanation_en: Best practices should come from credible, evidence-based quality organizations, then be adapted locally.
questions.explanation_ar: اعتمد على أدلة مبنية على البراهين من جهات معترف بها مثل CDC وIHI.

questions.task_name: Apply standards, best practices, and other information from quality-related organizations
questions.stem: Evidence-based practice integrates which three elements?

options.A: Regulations, budgets, and staffing levels set by leadership
options.B: Cost, speed, and convenience for the organization and its staff
options.C: Research evidence, clinical expertise, and patient values
options.D: Tradition, seniority, and existing organizational policy

questions.explanation_en: Evidence-based practice combines research evidence, clinician expertise, and patient preferences.
questions.explanation_ar: الممارسة المبنية على البراهين تجمع الدليل والخبرة وقيم المريض.

questions.task_name: Apply standards, best practices, and other information from quality-related organizations
questions.stem: A hospital's raw surgical mortality is higher than a peer hospital's, but it performs complex transplants the peer does not. A board member concludes surgical care is worse. What is the BEST response?

options.A: Stop publishing mortality data until the surgeons' results improve
options.B: Exclude transplant patients from the data
options.C: Agree and launch a disciplinary review of the surgical department
options.D: Explain that outcomes need case-mix risk adjustment first

questions.explanation_en: Unadjusted outcome comparisons across different case mixes are misleading; risk-adjust first.
questions.explanation_ar: لا تقارن النتائج قبل تعديلها وفق شدة الحالات.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: clinical practice guidelines, pathways, and outcomes
questions.stem: Compliance with a VTE-prophylaxis order set is 62%. Chart review shows many patients had documented contraindications. What should be done with these cases?

options.A: Delete the contraindicated patients from the medical record
options.B: Count documented contraindications as measure exclusions
options.C: Count all of them as non-compliant to stay conservative
options.D: Stop using the order set because compliance is too low

questions.explanation_en: Justified, documented clinical exceptions should be built into the measure definition so compliance reflects true performance.
questions.explanation_ar: الاستثناءات السريرية الموثقة تُستبعد من المقياس وفق تعريفه.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: clinical practice guidelines, pathways, and outcomes
questions.stem: Which tool embeds a clinical pathway into daily workflow at the point of ordering?

options.A: Patient satisfaction survey
options.B: Standardized EHR order set
options.C: Annual policy and procedure review
options.D: Incident reporting and trending system

questions.explanation_en: Order sets and protocols operationalize pathways where clinicians make decisions.
questions.explanation_ar: مجموعات الطلبات القياسية تدمج المسار السريري في العمل اليومي.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: clinical practice guidelines, pathways, and outcomes
questions.stem: Pathway variance analysis shows most delays in discharge are due to weekend unavailability of physical therapy. How should this variance be classified and addressed?

options.A: System variance; fix weekend PT coverage
options.B: Patient variance; no action
options.C: Random variance; ignore it because delays are expected
options.D: Practitioner variance; counsel the attending physicians

questions.explanation_en: System-driven variances (resources, scheduling) are the main targets for process redesign.
questions.explanation_ar: هذا انحراف نظامي يُعالج بتحسين تغطية العلاج الطبيعي.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: clinical practice guidelines, pathways, and outcomes
questions.stem: Which outcome measure would BEST evaluate whether a new heart failure pathway is effective?

options.A: Percentage of staff trained on the new pathway
options.B: Number of pathway copies printed and distributed
options.C: Number of pathway committee meetings held this year
options.D: Risk-adjusted 30-day heart failure readmission rate

questions.explanation_en: Effectiveness is judged by patient outcomes, not activities or outputs.
questions.explanation_ar: فعالية المسار تُقاس بالنتائج مثل معدل إعادة الدخول.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: quality-based payment programs
questions.stem: A program that pays a hospital only for submitting quality data, regardless of results, is called what?

options.A: Pay-for-performance
options.B: Pay-for-reporting
options.C: Bundled payment
options.D: Capitation

questions.explanation_en: Pay-for-reporting rewards data submission; pay-for-performance rewards results.
questions.explanation_ar: الدفع مقابل الإبلاغ يكافئ تقديم البيانات لا النتائج.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: quality-based payment programs
questions.stem: A hospital is in the worst-performing quartile for hospital-acquired conditions and faces a payment reduction. Which program applies?

options.A: Pay-for-reporting under inpatient quality reporting
options.B: Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS)
options.C: Hospital-Acquired Condition Reduction Program
options.D: Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program (HRRP)

questions.explanation_en: HACRP reduces payment for hospitals in the worst-performing quartile on HAC measures.
questions.explanation_ar: برنامج HACRP يعاقب المستشفيات الأسوأ ربعاً في الحالات المكتسبة.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: quality-based payment programs
questions.stem: The Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS) adjusts payments for which group?

options.A: Nursing homes only
options.B: Pharmaceutical companies
options.C: Acute care hospitals
options.D: Eligible clinicians

questions.explanation_en: MIPS is a clinician program under the Quality Payment Program, not a hospital program.
questions.explanation_ar: برنامج MIPS يخص الأطباء والممارسين وليس المستشفيات.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: quality-based payment programs
questions.stem: Under a bundled payment for hip replacement, the hospital receives one fixed payment covering 90 days. Which improvement focus offers the GREATEST financial and quality benefit?

options.A: Extending inpatient length of stay to monitor every patient longer
options.B: Reducing complications, readmissions, and excess post-acute care
options.C: Performing more imaging before discharge to detect complications
options.D: Increasing the number of lab tests per patient during the episode

questions.explanation_en: In bundles the provider bears the cost of complications, so preventing them improves both quality and margin.
questions.explanation_ar: في الدفع المجمّع تقليل المضاعفات وإعادة الدخول يحسن الجودة والعائد.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: documentation
questions.stem: A clinical documentation integrity (CDI) specialist finds 'sepsis' documented without supporting clinical indicators. What is the BEST action?

options.A: Ignore it; coding is not a quality issue
options.B: Code it as sepsis anyway, since this increases the case acuity
options.C: Send a compliant, non-leading query to the physician
options.D: Change the diagnosis in the record directly to match the indicators

questions.explanation_en: CDI queries must be non-leading and seek clinical clarification; altering records or upcoding is noncompliant.
questions.explanation_ar: يُرسل استفسار غير موجّه للطبيب لتوضيح التشخيص.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: documentation
questions.stem: A pressure injury documented as 'not present on admission' that develops during the stay is MOST likely to affect what?

options.A: HAC reporting and related payment
options.B: Nurse staffing ratio calculations for the unit
options.C: Emergency department triage level assignment
options.D: Admission priority and bed placement decisions

questions.explanation_en: POA = N flags the condition as hospital-acquired, affecting HAC measures and payment.
questions.explanation_ar: تسجيل الحالة كغير موجودة عند الدخول يجعلها مكتسبة ويؤثر على الدفع.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: documentation
questions.stem: A chart audit finds that 30% of records lack a signed informed-consent form before procedures. What is the BEST next step?

options.A: Analyze where the consent process breaks down and redesign it
options.B: Add the forms after the procedure
options.C: Stop auditing consent forms because the results are discouraging
options.D: Discipline all proceduralists with missing forms in their records

questions.explanation_en: Documentation gaps are process problems; analyze and redesign before blaming. Backdating is unethical.
questions.explanation_ar: حلل خطوات العملية لمعرفة سبب نقص التوثيق وأعد تصميمها.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: documentation
questions.stem: Which documentation practice BEST supports accurate risk-adjusted outcome reporting?

options.A: Using unapproved abbreviations so that notes are faster to write
options.B: Complete, specific documentation of comorbidities and severity
options.C: Using copy-paste notes from prior admissions to save clinician time
options.D: Documenting only the principal diagnosis to keep records concise

questions.explanation_en: Risk models depend on specific, complete documentation of comorbidities.
questions.explanation_ar: التوثيق الكامل والدقيق للأمراض المصاحبة يدعم دقة تعديل المخاطر.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: practitioner performance evaluation
questions.stem: An experienced orthopedic surgeon's OPPE data show a complication rate triple that of peers over two quarters. What should happen NEXT?

options.A: Wait for the next reappointment cycle in two years to review it
options.B: Publish the surgeon's complication data to all medical staff
options.C: Initiate a time-limited FPPE
options.D: Revoke the surgeon's privileges immediately pending investigation

questions.explanation_en: OPPE concerns trigger an FPPE to evaluate the issue fairly before any privilege action.
questions.explanation_ar: ارتفاع مؤشرات OPPE يستدعي تقييماً مركزاً FPPE.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: practitioner performance evaluation
questions.stem: What is the difference between credentialing and privileging?

options.A: Privileging verifies education; credentialing grants procedures
options.B: Credentialing applies only to nurses; privileging only to physicians
options.C: They are the same process described with two different names
options.D: Credentialing checks qualifications; privileging grants procedures

questions.explanation_en: Credentialing checks licensure, training, and experience; privileging defines the scope of practice granted.
questions.explanation_ar: الاعتماد يتحقق من المؤهلات، والامتيازات تحدد الإجراءات المسموح بها.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: practitioner performance evaluation
questions.stem: A peer review committee finds that a physician's case outcome was poor but care met the standard and the complication was a known risk. What is the MOST appropriate determination?

options.A: Care appropriate; no individual action, but track trends
options.B: Refer the physician to the licensing board for investigation
options.C: Care inappropriate, because the patient's outcome was poor
options.D: Require the physician to complete retraining before operating again

questions.explanation_en: Peer review judges the care process against standards, not the outcome alone (avoid outcome bias).
questions.explanation_ar: مراجعة الأقران تقيّم الرعاية مقابل المعايير لا النتيجة وحدها.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: patient experience
questions.stem: HCAHPS scores for 'communication about medicines' are low. What is the BEST improvement strategy?

options.A: Give patients the printed manufacturer drug inserts only
options.B: Survey only the patients who appear satisfied at discharge
options.C: Use teach-back to explain the purpose and side effects of new drugs
options.D: Remove the medication questions from the survey instrument

questions.explanation_en: Targeted communication behaviors linked to the survey domain improve the patient's experience.
questions.explanation_ar: تثقيف المريض عن الدواء وآثاره باستخدام إعادة الشرح يحسن التجربة.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: patient experience
questions.stem: A unit's patient-experience scores rose after staff began handing surveys only to patients who seemed happy. What is the main problem?

options.A: The sample is too large
options.B: Selection bias makes the results invalid
options.C: The survey is too short
options.D: The improvement is real and should be celebrated

questions.explanation_en: Selective distribution biases the sample; standardized random sampling is required.
questions.explanation_ar: توزيع الاستبيان انتقائياً يسبب تحيزاً ويُبطل النتائج.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: patient experience
questions.stem: Which statement about patient grievances is correct?

options.A: Grievances need a defined process, timelines, and a written reply
options.B: Grievances are handled informally by whichever staff member hears them
options.C: Grievances are optional to track if the patient is later satisfied
options.D: Only complaints submitted in writing can be classified as grievances

questions.explanation_en: Grievance processes include defined timeframes and written notice of the outcome.
questions.explanation_ar: التظلمات تتطلب إجراءات محددة ومواعيد وردّاً مكتوباً للمريض.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: identification of reportable events for accreditation and regulatory bodies
questions.stem: An infant is discharged to the wrong family. How should this event be handled for reporting purposes?

options.A: Treat it as a near miss because the infant was physically unharmed
options.B: Report only if the family complains
options.C: Treat it as a sentinel event and report as required
options.D: Handle it informally between the nurses involved on the unit

questions.explanation_en: Discharge of an infant to the wrong family is on The Joint Commission's list of sentinel events regardless of harm.
questions.explanation_ar: تسليم الرضيع لعائلة خاطئة حدث جسيم يتطلب الإبلاغ.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: identification of reportable events for accreditation and regulatory bodies
questions.stem: A hospital learns that state law requires reporting of a wrong-site surgery within 24 hours, while its accreditor encourages but does not require reporting. What is the BEST approach?

options.A: Report only to the accreditor, which oversees surgical safety
options.B: Wait until the RCA is complete before reporting to anyone
options.C: Report to the state within 24 hours; follow accreditor review rules
options.D: Report to neither, because the patient recovered from the surgery

questions.explanation_en: Mandatory regulatory reporting is required independently; accreditor policies are additional.
questions.explanation_ar: الإبلاغ الإلزامي للدولة واجب خلال المدة المحددة بغض النظر عن الاعتماد.

questions.task_name: Evaluate compliance: identification of reportable events for accreditation and regulatory bodies
questions.stem: Which of the following is generally NOT classified as a sentinel event?

options.A: Unintended retention of a foreign object after surgery
options.B: Wrong-site surgery
options.C: A medication error caught before reaching the patient
options.D: Patient suicide in a staffed care setting

questions.explanation_en: Near misses do not reach the patient and are not sentinel events, although they should be reported internally.
questions.explanation_ar: الخطأ الذي اكتُشف قبل وصوله للمريض حدث وشيك وليس جسيماً.

questions.task_name: Maintain confidentiality of performance/quality improvement records and reports
questions.stem: A plaintiff's attorney requests copies of a hospital's peer review minutes. What is the quality professional's FIRST step?

options.A: Summarize the minutes in the patient's chart for the attorney
options.B: Send the minutes promptly to avoid a court order
options.C: Destroy the minutes before they can be subpoenaed
options.D: Refer the request to legal counsel to protect privilege

questions.explanation_en: Peer review privilege must be protected through legal counsel; disclosure or destruction is inappropriate.
questions.explanation_ar: أحِل الطلب للمستشار القانوني لتطبيق الحماية القانونية.

questions.task_name: Maintain confidentiality of performance/quality improvement records and reports
questions.stem: A quality analyst wants to share a falls dashboard with an external collaborative. What should be done?

options.A: Refuse to share any data externally
options.B: Share aggregate de-identified data under a data-use agreement
options.C: Share the full patient list with names so results can be validated
options.D: Email the dashboard from a personal account to avoid the firewall

questions.explanation_en: External sharing should be de-identified and governed by agreements to protect privacy.
questions.explanation_ar: شارك بيانات مجمّعة ومجهولة الهوية ضمن اتفاقية استخدام.

questions.task_name: Maintain confidentiality of performance/quality improvement records and reports
questions.stem: The Health Care Quality Improvement Act (HCQIA) of 1986 is BEST known for what?

options.A: Creating Patient Safety Organizations and federal privilege
options.B: Peer review immunity and creating the NPDB
options.C: Establishing the HIPAA privacy and security rules
options.D: Requiring emergency screening and stabilization

questions.explanation_en: HCQIA gives immunity to good-faith peer review and created the NPDB.
questions.explanation_ar: قانون HCQIA يمنح الحصانة لمراجعة الأقران بحسن نية وأنشأ بنك بيانات الممارسين.

questions.task_name: Implement and evaluate quality initiatives that impact reimbursement
questions.stem: A readmission-reduction program cost SAR 300,000 and avoided SAR 900,000 in penalties and readmission costs. What is the ROI?
questions.explanation_ar: العائد = (الفائدة − التكلفة) ÷ التكلفة = 200%.

questions.task_name: Implement and evaluate quality initiatives that impact reimbursement
questions.stem: Which is an example of the cost of poor quality?

options.A: Extra stay caused by a hospital-acquired infection
options.B: Purchase of standard supplies at negotiated contract prices
options.C: Annual staff training budget for mandatory education
options.D: Routine preventive maintenance of biomedical equipment

questions.explanation_en: Cost of poor quality includes rework, complications, and failures such as HAIs.
questions.explanation_ar: تكلفة الجودة الرديئة تشمل الإقامة الإضافية بسبب العدوى المكتسبة.

questions.task_name: Implement and evaluate quality initiatives that impact reimbursement
questions.stem: A hospital wants to show leadership how a CAUTI project affected reimbursement. Which measure set is MOST useful?

options.A: CAUTI trend, avoided cost per case, and HAC penalty change
options.B: Number of CAUTI committee meetings held during the year
options.C: Hours spent by the infection preventionist on the project
options.D: Number of urinary catheters purchased compared with last year

questions.explanation_en: Financial impact links outcome change to avoided costs and penalties, not activity counts.
questions.explanation_ar: اربط تغيّر النتيجة بالتكاليف والغرامات المتجنبة لا بعدد الأنشطة.
